messages:
Sam: heads-up — noticed a perf regression on the latest TP/quant patch when running multi-GPU inference with KV cache warm. latency p50 +12% on 8xA100, p95 +22%. profile attached in-thread below. :ambulance:
Jess: ugh, when did this land? PR #1427? :thinking:
Sam: yep merged ~2hrs ago. It changes kernel selection for fused-attn and switches default qint8 kernel on TP shards. quick snapshot from local perf-run:
```
run: ./run_infer --model resnet-chat-v1 --gpus 8 --tp 2 --quant int8
p50: 45.3ms -> 50.7ms
p95: 110.8ms -> 135.4ms
tokens/s: 1784 -> 1560
```
Also seeing NCCL all-reduce spikes during kv flush; timing suggests comm blocking during last token for long contexts.
Miguel: can you paste the nvprof timeline? is the all-reduce happening inline or in a separate stream?
Sam: nvprof snippet:
```
[0.0s] kernel:fused_attn_fp8_select  duration 0.9ms  stream 2
[0.9s] NCCL_Allreduce          duration 3.1ms  stream 0
[4.0s] kernel:kv_write         duration 1.2ms  stream 2
(loops)
```
Streams show kernel compute on stream 2 and NCCL on 0 but we don't see overlap — suspect CPU-side kernel selection path serialized the launch order.
Lee: two things to check: 1) kernel-launch ordering when using per-shard quantized kernels (we had a bug that forces sync before NCCL if allocator touched tensors), 2) FP8 scale updates: if scale tensors are on CPU for TP shards, that causes implicit sync.
Jess: also noticed increased memory churn in the kv cache path — some temp tensors are getting created per request because of the new batching heuristic. Could be forcing reorder.
Sam: good catch. I ran a flamegraph; allocator alloc/free spikes align with the NCCL peaks.
Miguel: for comm/compute overlap: we should ensure NCCL calls go on the same stream as compute or on a comm stream that doesn't wait on host side. In TP mode we use per-rank streams; maybe the quant kernel uses cudaStreamSynchronize internally. Any sync calls in the new kernel wrapper?
Sam: searching the patch — there is an explicit `cudaDeviceSynchronize()` added in kernel_selector.cc to ensure reliable timing for microbenchmarks. That would wreck overlap in prod. PR description said it was temporary but got merged.
Lee: oh no. That explains everything. Remove that and re-run. Also confirm FP8 scaling tensors moved to GPU memory and use atomic updates rather than host roundtrips.
Jess: after removing the sync locally: p50 back to 46.1ms, p95 112.2ms. still ~2% up vs. baseline.
Miguel: small delta might be quant kernel math changes — INT8 rounding or different kernel tiling affecting occupancy. We should run microbench of fused_attn variants with `--tp=2` to compare kernels. Use `nvprof --profile-from-start off --trace-kernels` and the microbench harness.
Sam: ran microbench: fused_attn_qint8_v2 is slightly slower on short sequences but faster on long sequences (batching threshold change). That means batching heuristic flip could be causing more short-batch cases.
Lee: where is the batching heuristic change? I remember we altered `batch_split_threshold=64 -> 32` in the TP-specific path to improve throughput. That will increase number of micro-batches for short requests — higher kernel launch overhead.
Jess: yeah the commit `opt/batch-tuning` lowered threshold to reduce token latency for large batches, but in TP mode the kernel launch cost is amplified. We should make the threshold conditional on TP/shard count.
Miguel: action items: 1) revert cudaDeviceSynchronize in kernel selector, 2) move FP8 scale tensors to GPU and use per-thread scaling (avoid CPU sync), 3) add TP-aware batching_threshold, 4) run CI perf suite (8-gpu).
Sam: infra-bot kicked off the perf CI: job 44321 starting — measuring p50/p95/tokens/s against baseline.
infra-bot: perf-ci:job:44321 started by Sam. testing branch: fix/tp-quant-kv-sync.
Jess: I also want to add a regression test: run 50 short requests with kv warm across TP=2,4 and assert p95 < 1.15x baseline. Otherwise fail the merge gate.
Lee: good. One more: add kernel-selection logging at debug level for TP so we can see which fused_attn kernel was picked per-shard. That will help correlate. Keep logs off by default.
Miguel: note on FP8/INT8 scaling: we observed occasional output divergence for certain prompt patterns when scaling used per-layer global max rather than per-head; that change was in the quant patch. Need to test quality after these perf fixes. If INT8/FP8 scaling reverts quality, we might need hybrid fallback (use fp16 for sensitive layers).
Sam: agreed — will add evals run on the regression harness (1000 prompts) after perf passes. Also will instrument KV cache path to avoid temporary allocations: reuse preallocated per-request buffer in TP mode.
Jess: thanks. once infra-ci results are in, let's sync in the eng-runtime standup. :eyes:
Sam: infra-ci completed: job 44321 results:
```
p50: 46.0ms (baseline 45.3ms)
p95: 113.1ms (baseline 110.8ms)
tokens/s: 1768 (baseline 1784)
```
So most regression fixed; still a small delta. I'm suspecting kernel tiling/occupancy differences from qint8 kernel.
Miguel: acceptable for now, but open follow-up to dig into kernel occupancy and try launching with different block dims. Also schedule a micro-kernel profiling session with Nsight next week.
Lee: created follow-up ticket INF-879: "TP quant kernel occupancy + batching tuning" and assigned to Miguel.
Sam: thanks all. I'll revert the sync immediately and land TP-aware batching change. Will post update once evals complete. :thumbsup:
